newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares rise 1.84 pct in limited recovery.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares rise 1.84 pct in limited recovery.

text.p: Istanbul shares regained part of Tuesday's sharp losses in a limited recovery on Wednesday, but fell from earlier highs amid caution due to ongoing political worries, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed 27 points, or 1.84 percent, higher at 1,492 but below a morning high of 1,516. It had plunged 6.98 percent yesterday amid political worries and higher-than-expected January inflation data.
Trade volume firmed to 26.60 trillion lira from Tuesday's 22.79 trillion.

"Political developments concerning the coalition government have unnerved the market although they are not seen strong enough to lead to a breakup in the coalition," said Hakan Aksoy from Alfa securities.

The market was depressed by reported uneasiness in the Islamist-led coalition's conservative wing over last Friday's Islamist protest and censure motions filed by two leftist parties against the government.
Brokers said selling began in the afternoon ahead of a parliamentary vote following the morning's 3.28 percent jump caused by selective buys in bluechips.

Reviewing a vote against setting up an inquiry into Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller on corruption charges, the parliament rejected the opposition proposal. The rejection caused shares to post more gains towards the close.
The index had lost 13.82 percent by Tuesday's close from the previous Monday's all-time high of 1,700, after surging 74.2 percent and hitting 17 record closes from end-1996 to January 27.

"Last month's strong uptrend seems to be over although the index may again rebound to 1,550-1,600 range. There won't be as strong a liquidity influx. Consolidation is normal after such a steep rally," said Aksoy.
Brokers said an approaching holiday also discouraged buying this week as Turkish investors mostly place their money in repo deals during long holidays.
Turkish markets will be closed next Monday and Tuesday due to the Moslem end of Ramadan holiday and will reopen on February 12.
Brokers expect some buying on Thursday and Friday because settlements of transactions will be delayed to after the holiday.

Of the 239 issues traded, rises outdid falls by 155 to 43 and 41 closed unchanged. The IMKB Industrial firmed 2.17 percent to 1,553, the IMKB Services edged up 0.28 percent to 1,417 and the IMKB Financial gained 2.02 percent to 1,462.

Actives were led by largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, up 500 lira at 21,500, T.Isbank's C series, up 500 lira at 30,500 and utilities Cukurova Elektrik, up 2,500 lira at 212,500 and Aktas Elektrik, up 7,500 lira at 177,500.
They made up 28.3 percent of the total volume.
